observations: Photo 0: Silver-top retro SLR-style mirrorless body, 'Nikon' logo and 'Zfc' lettering visible on top plate and front, rear lens cap marked 'Nikon Z mount' attached (no lens mounted in this shot).

Photo 1: Close-up of top dials (ISO dial numbers 100-51200, shutter speed markings) and 'Nikon Zfc' engraving; a manual-focus lens is mounted, its aperture ring engraved '1.8' and distance scale visible, barrel marked with a maker name partly obscured by watermark.

Photo 2: Top-down flat-lay showing the camera body with lens attached, a Nikon-branded rechargeable battery, a Nikon battery charger, two body/rear caps, and a separate lens cap marked 'TTArtisan APS-C 25mm F2.0'.
No photo shows the rear LCD screen, viewfinder display, a power-on state, a memory card slot, or any image/video captured by the camera.
No shot of the lens mount contacts or sensor; mount is covered by a cap in photo 0.
Watermark 'OYIBEST GLOBAL RESOURCES' overlays all images; no serial number or date stamp visible in any photo.

claims.claim: Nikon Z fc is a retro-inspired, SLR-style mirrorless camera
claims.evidence: photo 0 and photo 1 show the Nikon Zfc branding and SLR-style pentaprism-shaped housing
No sensor, spec sheet, or camera menu screen is shown in any photo; this is a published spec for the real Zfc but cannot be confirmed as the actual unit's sensor from photos alone

claims.claim: (Implied) camera is in working condition / comes complete with kit
claims.evidence: No power-on, screen, or shutter-fire evidence; battery and charger shown in photo 2 but no proof of charging or camera turning on

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or have a functioning shutter/sensor
risks.proof: A video clip of the camera powering on, showing the rear LCD/EVF live view and a test shot playback

risks.risk: Lens mounted is a third-party TTArtisan 25mm f2.0 manual lens, not an original Nikkor Z kit lens, which lowers bundle value versus a 'with kit lens' listing
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the lens barrel engraving confirming TTArtisan branding (partially visible in photo 2 cap) and confirmation no Nikkor lens is included
risks.if_unproven: priced as body + generic manual lens, not an official Nikon kit lens

risks.risk: Shutter count / usage history unknown, could be heavily used despite cosmetic appearance
risks.proof: Screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or EXIF data of a sample photo

risks.risk: Possible mount or sensor damage hidden by cap, or body could be a refurbished/gray-market unit
risks.proof: Photo of the lens mount with cap off showing contacts and sensor area, plus serial number photo matched to Nikon's database
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming mount/sensor condition unverified, worst case

risks.risk: No memory card or card slot shown, buyer may need to assume no card door compatibility issues
risks.if_unproven: treated as body-only sale, card not included

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, showing menu/live view and a test shutter actuation
Photo of the lens mount with cap removed, showing contacts and sensor
Photo of the serial number sticker/plate for authenticity check
Confirmation/photo of shutter count or EXIF data from a recent photo
Clear unobstructed photo of the lens barrel to confirm it is the TTArtisan 25mm f2.0 and not a Nikkor lens
response.reason: The body is clearly identifiable as a Nikon Z fc from the engravings in photos 0-2, but no photo proves it powers on, fires a shutter, or that the mount/sensor are undamaged, and the attached lens is a third-party TTArtisan unit rather than an original Nikkor kit lens, so it must be priced at worst case as an unproven-working body with a non-original lens.
